tests:
- **Whole suite, at `2d60cdd3` plus the new file: 58 failed, 388 passed, 0 skipped.**
- A single run of the whole folder hit the time limit of a foreground call twice (exit 124, about 10–11 minutes). So I ran the same command line five times, each file once, never with `-x`:

| Files | Result |
|---|---|
| `extra_review` | 72 passed |
| `short_round` + `last_review` | 78 passed |
| `code_under_test`, `guard_own_folder`, `guard_refusals`, `launcher`, `review_findings` | 187 passed |
| `never_indexed` + `owner_answers` | 21 passed |
| `link_replaced` (new) | 58 failed, 30 passed |

- **Red reason** for all 58: "Bash `…` (<case>; it replaces the link … -> …, <place>) was not refused: decision=allow". Today's guard judges the link's target, not the link it replaces.
- **D cases (60)**, each named `<form>--<place>`. The places are: the acceptance folder, another ticket's folder with a link into the session's own folder, and, for a few, an allowed folder holding a link to an allowed file.
  - `cp` with a backup (17): `-b`, `--backup`, `=simple`, `=numbered`, `-S.t`, `--suffix=.bak`, `-bS .t`, `-b -S .t`, `-b -f`, `-b -t` (including the review's `cp -b -t W2-91 mylink`), `--backup -t`, `-b -T`, `-b --`.
  - `--remove-destination` (6): including `--rem`, `--remove` and with `-t`.
  - `cp -f` / `--force` (7): onto a link to a read-only file (the tool replaces it), onto a link to a writable file (the form may replace), and onto a dangling link.
  - `install` (9): plain, `-m 644`, `-b`, `-t`, `-T`, `-D`.
  - `mv` (9): plain, `-f`, `-b`, `-T`, `-t`, `--`.
  - `-T` onto a link to a folder (4): `mv`, `install`, `cp -b`.
  - A source that is itself a link (4): `cp -P`, `-a`, `-R`, `--no-dereference`.
  - A link moved away (4): `mv <link> <own folder>/x`, in several forms.
- **Passing today, among the D cases (2):** `mv-t--acceptance` and `mv-t--other-ticket`. The guard already refuses them because it names the `-t` folder itself. They must stay refused.
- **Controls (28), all passing:**
  - Plain `cp` and `cp -t` writing through a link to an allowed file (6). This includes the link at a protected name, where the tool writes through to an allowed target.
  - `cp`, `cp -b`, `install`, `install -m 644` and `mv` into a link to a folder, or through one at a middle level (10). I checked that no tool replaces the link in these.
  - `cp -b`, `--remove-destination`, `cp -f`, `install` and `mv -b` onto ordinary files that are not links, in the repository and in the own folder (10).
  - A link moved between allowed folders (2).
- The existing cases that hold run 6's allows and refusals are named in the README rather than duplicated.

discoveries:
- **What each form does to a link (coreutils 9.4):**
  - These **replace** the link: `cp` with any backup option; `--remove-destination` and its prefixes (`--r` is refused as ambiguous); `cp -f` when the target is not writable; every `install` (even `-C` with equal content); every `mv`; `mv -T`, `install -T` and `cp -b -T` onto a link to a folder; `cp -P`, `-d`, `-a`, `-r`, `-R` when the source is itself a link.
  - These **follow** the link: plain `cp` and most other `cp` options with a regular source; `cp -f` when the target is writable; `--backup=none` and `--backup=off`; every form into a link to a folder.
  - `cp -f` onto a dangling link does **not** replace it: the tool refuses with "not writing through dangling symlink". `cp -s` and `cp -l` fail onto an existing file.
- **`mv -t <folder>` is judged as the folder itself**, while `cp -t` and `install -t` are judged as each file they write.
- **Today `mv <elsewhere>/X <link>` is refused because of its source**, so the move cases use sources in `src/app/staging/`.
- **No earlier case of this suite or of another ticket conflicts with D**: none asks that a form which replaces a link be allowed. I checked W1-02, W1-03, W1-07, W1-19, W1-39, W1-40, W1-46, W1-48 and W1-50.

risks:
- **How the "doubt" refusal is checked.** Each case first takes the path that an `ln -t` refusal into an allowed folder names (today `/<guard-unresolvable>`). Cases in an allowed folder must name that exact path. Cases at a protected name may name it, the link's own path, or the link's folder. If an engineer reports doubt some other way, the allowed-folder cases go red.
- **Cases that are stricter than what the tool does.** `cp -f` onto a link to a writable allowed file, and `cp -f` onto a dangling link, must be refused because the form may replace. The tool itself does not replace in either case. That follows the brief's text.

lessons:
- The whole folder (446 cases) no longer fits in one foreground call. Run it in the five groups above.
- Move sources must sit in the session's own paths, or the refusal you see is the source's, not the destination's.

proposed_decisions: none

unresolved:
- Whether `cp --backup=none` / `--backup=off` onto a link should be allowed (they follow it) is untested either way.
- Refusing `cp -a`, `-P` or `-R` onto any link, whatever the source, would be stricter than D. That is not tested against.

recommended_next_action: Hand the 58 red cases to the engineer for the D round; it is done when all 446 cases pass, run in the five groups.
